Ingredion approached Penford on July 17, 2014 and subsequently signed a secrecy agreement. Its proposed price rose from $17.00 on August 6 to $18.00 in cash on August 10. Penford refused exclusivity and authorized a market check on August 28. Deutsche Bank contacted six strategic counterparties, and Parties A, C and D signed confidentiality agreements. After Ingredion increased its price to $19.00, the board selected it for definitive negotiations on October 3 while continuing to seek a letter from Party A. Party A ultimately proposed $16.00, and Penford signed with Ingredion for $19.00 in cash on October 14 and announced the merger the next day.
